correctness.rationale: Direct exponent cancellation proves K invariance. Monotonicity of K y^alpha+alpha y gives the unique leafwise fixed point; lambda=1-R+(alpha-1)y_K decreases through -1 exactly at x+y=2. For lambda<-1, f_K^2(y)-y is positive just above zero and negative just below the equilibrium, proving an actual positive nonconstant two-cycle by IVT. At the crossing the second derivative is -t/y_c and the third derivative is [4+(5-alpha)t]/y_c^2, giving flip cubic c=Q/(12y_c^2); the smooth scalar normal form gives attracting/repelling cycle types on the stated sides. Independently checked rational supercritical and subcritical witnesses by direct finite differences and exact Q arithmetic. The planar fixed point has neutral multiplier one, so no full-plane attraction is asserted.
residual_risks: At Q=0 the cubic flip criterion vanishes; no higher-order type or global cycle uniqueness is proved.

value.rationale: The result resolves a motivated degenerate parameter locus excluded by generic planar flip theory, exhibits every postthreshold leaf having a positive cycle, and sharply partitions supercritical and subcritical behavior by a nontrivial competition-strength threshold; not just a parameter substitution.
residual_risks: Cycles on different invariant leaves are not asymptotically stable in the full plane, and global enumeration is open.

final_claim: On the exactly aligned two-species Ricker family alpha>1, 2<R<2alpha, K=x/y^alpha is invariant; each K>Kc supports a positive two-cycle, with leafwise flip type determined by Q(alpha,t)=3t^2+2(5-alpha)t+8 and subcritical Q<0 iff alpha>5+2sqrt(6).
limitations: Only exactly aligned alpha beta=1 and S=R/alpha, strictly positive populations, not arbitrary Ricker competition.
